{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Soyuz TMA-4 was a Soyuz mission to the International Space Station (ISS) launched by a Soyuz FG launch vehicle.","title":"Soyuz TMA-4"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It was launched on April 19, 2004 (UTC) from Baikonur Cosmodrome.","title":"Soyuz TMA-4"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" Gennady Padalka from Russia, Michael Fincke from the USA and André Kuipers from the Netherlands were flown to the International Space Station.","title":"Soyuz TMA-4"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" Kuipers returned to Earth 9 days later together with ISS crew 8 with the re-entry module of the Soyuz TMA-3, the other two stayed as ISS crew 9.","title":"Soyuz TMA-4"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" The craft landed October 24, 2004 with Padalka, Fincke and Yuri Shargin aboard.","title":"Soyuz TMA-4"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Scott Joseph Kelly (born February 21, 1964 in Orange, New Jersey) is an engineer, retired American astronaut, and a retired U.S. Navy Captain.","title":"Scott Kelly (astronaut)"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" A veteran of four space flights, Kelly commanded the International Space Station (ISS) on Expeditions 26, 45, and 46.","title":"Scott Kelly (astronaut)"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":null,"question":"Although Michael Fincke's record was broken by Scott Kelly, commander of the International Space Station (ISS) on Expeditions 26, 45, and 46, what was his record for the most time in space?"}
